summary: This RFC proposes a set of RFCs on how networking code is integrated into various operating systems, a topic the authors felt had been under-documented. It asks for comments and suggestions.

eli5.summary: Different computers need to learn the network's language in their own way. This asks people to write down how they did it.

questions: how to integrate networking code into operating systems
proposal for rfcs on networking in operating systems
os integration challenges for internet protocols
subtitle: A call to document how networks integrate with operating systems.

tldr.problem: Operating system vendors often resist making changes needed to support networking protocols, but the networking community has not documented how to successfully integrate network code into various operating systems, leaving implementation details scattered and undiscussed.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 967 proposes a new subseries of RFCs that would collect essays from implementers of each major operating system, describing how they integrated host-host protocol interpreters, subnet processors, device drivers, Telnet, and FTP into their OS.
tldr.outcome: This call for community documentation aims to help both OS vendors understand what networking requires and future implementers learn from past experience, using the RFC literature as an educational tool.

today: RFC 967 is Informational and remains an unfulfilled call for documentation. While some integration documentation emerged for specific systems, the comprehensive subseries of essays the author envisioned did not materialize. Modern cloud computing and containerization have changed how operating systems handle networking, though the fundamental tensions between networking requirements and OS design persist.

sections.title: The Documentation Gap
sections.content: RFC 967 observes that networking code, when properly integrated into an operating system, becomes system code and requires the kind of deep changes that OS vendors often resist. The RFC notes that this problem affects organizations across the industry, from academic research networks to major companies like IBM. The author proposes that the ARPANET community should document this integration process to help practitioners understand what is required and to justify these changes to OS vendors.
sections.eli5: Putting Internet tools into a computer means changing how the computer works. Different computers change in different ways. Nobody has written down how.

sections.title: A Subseries of RFCs
sections.content:
The author proposes a new subseries of RFCs focusing on OS integration, with essays from practitioners who have integrated networking code into each major operating system. Each essay should document the Host-Host protocol interpreter(s), the Subnet Processor device driver, Telnet integration, FTP integration (addressing whether it runs per-user or as a single daemon on the server), and relevant aspects of the OS architecture itself. The author offers to coordinate submissions and potentially help edit and merge overlapping contributions from different implementers on the same OS.

The goal is eventually to publish these essays in the open literature beyond the RFC series itself, making this knowledge available to a broader audience.
sections.eli5: Ask everyone who put the Internet on their computer to write an essay about it. Then collect them together so everyone can learn from everyone else.

sections.title: Striking Back at Objections
sections.content: The RFC frames this initiative as a way to "strike back" at OS vendors who object to necessary networking modifications by showing them what they should be including in their systems. The author notes that modern systems' trends toward making device drivers easier to add and offering interprocess communication primitives at the system level may simplify integration, though one remaining challenge is adapting the process creation path for Telnet. The author expresses hope that volunteers will document all major and most minor operating systems on the network, creating a comprehensive handbook of integration experience.
sections.eli5: If we show the computer makers what networking really needs, maybe they'll make their computers easier to network.

references.text: Padlipsky, M. A., "Introduction to some proposed Standards for use in the Internet", RFC 928, December 1985.
